newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania moves to use bourse, OTC for privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Romania moves to use bourse, OTC for privatisation.

text.p: Romania's government moved on Saturday to empower the country's main privatisation agency to use the local capital markets to sell some 1,000 state companies by the end of this year.

Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu said the government had adopted a decree allowing the State Ownership Fund (FPS) to sell its majority stake in the firms up for quick privatisation on the bourse or the over-the-counter (OTC) market.
"This decree sets the legal basis for the FPS' plans to sell off its stake through the capital markets," Spineanu told a news conference.

FPS president Sorin Dimitriu had previously revealed plans to put some 60 companies on sale on the Bucharest stock exchange. It would also use special trades on the local OTC market to privatise at least five companies per day.
The FPS has a controlling stake in more than 6,500 state firms up for eventual privatisation.

The new centrist government has pledged to speed up privatisation of large sectors of the economy. Of more than 6,500 firms slated for privatisation in 1992, some 3,100 had been sold by the end of 1996.
